# Documentation Index

Index for discovering relevant documents during Plan and Explore execution

## Usage

Identify and read task-related sections below:

- Modify `cmd/` or CLI behavior → Read **Specifications** section (CLI, Requirements)
- Modify YAML configuration handling → Read **Specifications** section (Configuration, Requirements)
- Make design decisions or evaluate scope → Read **Project Overview** section
- Edit documents under `docs/` → Read **Contributing** section

## Specifications

- [Requirements](docs/spec/requirements.md): Functional requirements, quality requirements, and invariants of reco - Use when implementing or changing features, or checking supported scope and safety guarantees
- [CLI](docs/spec/cli.md): Commands (`plan`, `apply`, `show`), options, credential selection, interactive approval, output, and exit codes - Use when modifying `cmd/`, adding commands or options, or changing user-visible output and exit codes
- [Configuration](docs/spec/configuration.md): YAML configuration structure, types, allowed values, combinations, management scope interpretation, and input validation - Use when modifying configuration parsing or validation, or adding supported repository settings

## Design

- [Domain Model](docs/design/domain.md): Core concepts of reco and the distinctions between them (declaration, selection, and repository identity; managed settings; current state vs. observation result and the points in time of observation; reconciliation vs. applicability; change plan structure; logical change vs. update operation; approval and change preconditions; the contexts each concept belongs to) - Use when naming domain types, deciding what a concept means, or checking that code keeps these distinctions
- [Architecture](docs/design/architecture.md): Logical components and their boundaries, change planning and execution control, pre-validation, approval and per-update precondition checks, GitHub API trust boundary (redirects, unmanaged-setting preservation, non-atomic updates), and result classification - Use when placing responsibilities across packages, implementing the plan/apply flow, or changing how GitHub updates are issued and verified

## Research

- [Research](docs/research/README.md): Purpose of the GitHub API research documents, how they are split, and the conventions they follow (grounded only in GitHub official docs, API version basis, developer-verified behavior as notes) - Use when adding a GitHub API fact or a new endpoint document
- [GitHub OpenAPI Excerpt](docs/research/openapi.json): Excerpt of GitHub's official OpenAPI 3.0 description limited to the operations reco uses and the components they reference, generated by `scripts/openapi/update.sh` - Use when checking request or response field types and enum values of an endpoint reco uses
- [GitHub REST API Common](docs/research/rest-api.md): GitHub REST API contract shared by every endpoint reco uses (request URL and headers, API versions, redirects, failure responses, rate limits, conditional requests, token types, scopes, and repository roles) - Use when a spec or design needs a GitHub fact that is not specific to one endpoint
- [GitHub Repositories API](docs/research/repositories.md): Repository get and update endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, merge-related field visibility, repository name vs. ID and rename redirects, general setting fields and update behavior) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about repository identity or general settings
- [GitHub Actions Permissions API](docs/research/actions-permissions.md): Actions permissions, selected actions, and workflow permissions endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, fields, update units, and observed side effects) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about GitHub Actions permission settings

## Project Overview

- [Constitution](docs/CONSTITUTION.md): Purpose, problem statement, value proposition, design principles, and non-goals of reco - Use when making design decisions, resolving tradeoffs between principles, or judging whether a feature is in scope

## Contributing

- [Documentation Policy](docs/contributing/docs-policy.md): Responsibilities and sources of truth of each document, identifiers (`FR`, `QR`, `INV`), Relationships (`alignment`, `grounding`, `checks`), and consistency checks on change - Use when adding or changing requirements, identifiers, or Relationship tables, or when editing specs and designs
